literal: Petty pleasure having coveted, unrighteous deeds they will indeed not do, the other pleasure those who desire.
translation: Those who desire the supreme, lasting bliss of virtue will not commit unrighteous deeds out of a desire for the petty, fleeting pleasure of coveting others' wealth.
modern: நிலையான உயர்ந்த இன்பத்தை விரும்புபவர்கள், பிறர் பொருளைக் கவர நினைக்கும் சிற்றின்பத்தை விரும்பி அறமற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்யமாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts two kinds of happiness: 'சிற்றின்பம்' (the petty, transient pleasure of coveting and taking what belongs to others) and 'மற்று இன்பம்' (the other, supreme and lasting bliss that comes from a life of virtue). Those who truly seek the higher, enduring happiness will never stoop to unrighteous acts. They understand that the small gain from covetousness is fleeting and ultimately destructive to their character.
